patch_description: Builds on the winning design's insight that aggressive parameter sharing (grouping qubits into pairs with shared RY/RZ angles) improves generalization and convergence speed. The novel contribution here is a **dual-ring entangling topology**: instead of a single nearest-neighbor CRZ ring, we alternate nearest-neighbor (distance-1) and next-nearest-neighbor (distance-2) CRZ couplings around the ring, each sharing just two parameters (crz_a, crz_b) across their respective ring positions. This creates richer, longer-range entanglement (distance-1 AND distance-2 connectivity) using the same tiny parameter count as the seed's single ring, since distance-2 connections let information mix across more distant qubits within one block — reducing the number of blocks/uploads needed to spread correlations across all 8 qubits. We keep the qubit-pair-grouped RY/RZ pre-rotation layer (4 shared angles each) that proved effective for both accuracy and generalization gap in the prior program, and retain the shared post-rotation RZ layer for phase realignment before the next feature upload. This keeps the parameter count essentially the same (88 vs 86) while giving the entangler more topological expressiveness per parameter, which should improve convergence speed and possibly closes the generalization gap further by giving the circuit more expressive, though still highly constrained (shared), interactions.
